outcome: The problem itself (minimum area of a convex universal cover for planar sets of diameter one) remains open, but the certified lower bound on the area moved three times in 2026, from the 2005 Brass–Sharifi value of 0.832 to 0.833 (Xie, June/July 2026), then to 0.834 (Zeng, September 2026) and 0.8344 (Mishra, August/September 2026); the upper bound is unchanged from Gibbs' 2018 preprint value of 0.8440935944.

ai.basis_quote: Large language models were used for language editing, formatting assistance, and consistency checks.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks for the minimum-area convex shape in the plane covering every diameter-one set (the 2D case). This remains open: no upper or lower bound closes the gap. But the lower bound on the area constant a_Leb moved three separate times within the window, all in 2026, all using the same basic strategy of exhibiting explicit convex test sets (a disc plus polygons or Reuleaux-type constant-width curves) and certifying, by exhaustive/interval-arithmetic computation, that their convex hull under all relative placements has area at least some threshold. Niantao Xie (arXiv:2606.04458, submitted 2026-06-03, v4 2026-07-08) reproduced/improved the Brass–Sharifi (2005, 0.832) framework to certify 0.833. Ujjwal Mishra (arXiv:2608.30538, submitted 2026-08, v2 2026-09-01) switched the test sets to curves of constant width (disc, Reuleaux triangle, Reuleaux pentagon) and an exhaustive subdivision of a 5-dimensional placement space (486,799,600 nodes, independently re-verified certificate) to reach 0.8344. Shuai Zeng (arXiv:2609.01284, submitted 2026-09-01) built an exact Reuleaux-type variational hierarchy with a proven O(M⁻²) convergence rate to the true constant, certifying 0.834 as a realization of one finite level of that hierarchy. None of these three papers has been digested by an expert commentator, accepted at a journal, or discussed on Tao's blog / Quanta / similar outlets as of the check date — they remain preprints, so the correct status is progress (a bound moved on a problem that stays open), not resolved or claimed. The upper bound side saw no movement in the window: the best known convex universal cover is still Gibbs' 2018 preprint value of area 0.8440935944, repeatedly cited unchanged across all three 2026 papers and by the current Wikipedia article. On AI: only Zeng's paper (2609.01284) makes any AI disclosure, and it is explicitly language-editing/formatting/consistency-checking, i.e. squarely `none` under §6.2 — the mathematics (the hierarchy, the convergence proof, the certificate) is presented as the author's own work verified by interval arithmetic, not produced by an AI system. Xie's and Mishra's papers make no AI disclosure at all. A fourth arXiv item flagged by triage, 'Note on Lebesgue's universal cover problem' (arXiv:2607.27227, Yizhen Chen), is about the 3-dimensional universal covering problem — a dodecahedron counterexample, volume bounds in R^3, and a polytope family in R^n — which changes the ambient dimension of the question and is therefore a related problem under §3.1, not a case of the stated (planar) bullet; it does not affect this record's status. A fifth item found independently, 'On asymptotic Lebesgue's universal covering problem' (arXiv:2512.04023, Arman/Bondarenko/Prymak/Radchenko, submitted 2025-12-03), proves Jung's ball is asymptotically volume-optimal among universal covers in R^n as n→∞ — again the high-dimensional asymptotic problem, a related problem, not the n=2 case asked about here, and also contains no AI disclosure. No priority dispute or retraction was found among the three lower-bound papers; each explicitly supersedes its immediate predecessor and cites it, forming a normal sequential improvement rather than a controversy.
competing_reading: One could argue the sequence of lower-bound papers, taken together, is significant enough progress (closing roughly a quarter of the 2005-era gap between 0.832 and 0.8441 within a single year) to warrant more weight than a routine `progress` tag conveys, but none of the three individual results is large enough or expert-vetted enough to justify `claimed` or `resolved`, and the underlying existence/value question (what is a_Leb exactly) is unchanged in kind, only in how tightly it is bracketed — consistent with §3.1's treatment of a moved bound as `progress` rather than a change to the core open question.
what_would_settle_it: A journal acceptance or an expert digestion (e.g. a Tao-blog or Quanta writeup, or citation/verification by another specialist in discrete/convex geometry) of any of the three 2026 lower-bound papers would move that paper's contribution from `progress`/preprint status toward `resolved`-quality confirmation of the specific bound (though the overall Lebesgue problem would still be open). Discovery of an AI-generated construction or proof step in any of these or a future paper would change the ai_role from `none`.
